{{nihongo|'''Suwa Shrine'''|諏訪神社 (美濃加茂市)}} is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|Q845945|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Minokamo, Gifu|Q857305|qid=Q857305}}, {{ill|Gifu Prefecture|Q131277|qid=Q131277}}. {{nihongo|'''Suwa Shrine'''|諏訪神社 (美濃加茂市)}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mino Province]].

It is a candidate shrine for Nakayama Shrine, a {{ill|Shikinaisha|lt=Shikinaisha|qid=Q134917286}} of {{ill|Kamo District, Gifu|Q1348656|qid=Q1348656|lt=Kamo District}}, {{ill|Mino Province|Q864156|qid=Q864156}} (the other candidate is {{ill|Nakayama Shrine (Q11364249)|Q11364249|qid=Q11364249|lt=Nakayama Shrine}}).

== History ==
The founding period is unknown. It is said to have originally stood at Nakayama in Shimo-Iida Village, Kamo District, Mino Province (present Shimo-Iida, {{ill|Kawabe, Gifu|Q1203748|qid=Q1203748}}, {{ill|Kamo District, Gifu|Q1348656|qid=Q1348656}}). Another theory says the location was that of current {{ill|Nakayama Shrine (Q11364249)|Q11364249|qid=Q11364249|lt=Nakayama Shrine}}.

It burned down in war during the {{ill|Eiroku|Q1143341|qid=Q1143341}} era. Later, by order of Hida Genba, lord of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yoneda Castle}}, Hida Chōjumaru rebuilt it at the present site. At that time, {{ill|Suwa-taisha|Q218813|qid=Q218813}} of {{ill|Shinano Province|Q289250|qid=Q289250}} was enshrined and the name was changed to Suwa Shrine.

On April 1, {{ill|1981|Q2437|qid=Q2437}} (Shōwa 56), it was designated by the Gifu Prefecture Association of Shinto Shrines as a chief-visit designated shrine ({{ill|Kinpei-sha|Q119929592|qid=Q119929592}}, designation No. Kin-84){{sfn|Kimura|1997|p=65}}.

== Annual festival ==
*Held every year on the first Saturday and Sunday of April.
:Two {{ill|danjiri|Q11271630|qid=Q11271630}} carrying statues of {{ill|Takeda Shingen|ar|تاكيدا شين-غن|az|Takeda Şingen|ban|Takeda Shingen|ca|Takeda Shingen|cs|Šingen Takeda|de|Takeda Shingen|eo|Takeda Shingen|es|Takeda Shingen|fa|تاکدا شینگن|fi|Takeda Shingen|fr|Takeda Shingen (daimyō)|hak|Takeda Shingen|he|טקדה שינגן|hu|Takeda Singen|id|Takeda Shingen|it|Takeda Shingen|ja|武田信玄|jv|Takeda Shingen|ko|다케다 신겐|nl|Takeda Shingen|no|Takeda Shingen|pl|Shingen Takeda|pt|Takeda Shingen|ru|Такэда Сингэн|sk|Šingen Takeda|sq|Takeda Shingen|sr|Такеда Шинген|sv|Takeda Shingen|th|ทาเกดะ ชิงเง็ง|tr|Takeda Shingen|uk|Такеда Шінґен|vi|Takeda Shingen|wuu|武田信玄|zh|武田信玄|zh_min_nan|Takeda Singen|zh_yue|武田信玄|zu|Takeda Shingen|qid=Q276404}} and {{ill|Uesugi Kenshin|Q311080|qid=Q311080}} are pulled through the approach. When they climb the slope and reach the shrine, Yoneda-bayashi music is played. During the procession, a {{ill|Lion dance|Q713866|qid=Q713866|lt=lion}} chases women watching, and a haiō figure wearing a tengu mask and holding {{ill|Cleyera japonica|Q775470|qid=Q775470}} branches restrains it.
:A dedicatory {{ill|Sumo|Q40561|qid=Q40561}} event is held.
